routes.name: Citizens of the United States (Compact of Free Association, as amended)

note: Federated States of Micronesia, read on 2026-10-30 in the FSM Information Services' release of 22 November 2005, 'FSM adopts new Immigration Regulation', as the Permanent Mission of the FSM to the United Nations publishes it (unmission.fm). The regulation in force from October 2005 replaced the 1986 version, to be consistent with the immigration laws (Title 50 of the FSM Code, as amended by Public Law 12-65) and the amended Compact. Under the Compact, citizens of the United States are exempt from all entry permit fees and have the right to reside, work and do business in the FSM without any further immigration document and needn't register their presence (written as free movement for the US, work any; where they 'apply' isn't asked, so it isn't written). Other non-citizens hold entry permits, may change their entry permit status by a set procedure, and pay fees for entry permits, whose amounts the release doesn't give; their kinds aren't named, so one `general` entry permit route is written. Citizens of the Marshall Islands and Palau have 'some exemptions' the release doesn't detail, so they aren't modelled apart. The 2005 regulation and Title 50 themselves weren't read: fsmlaw.org answered 406 (its ModSecurity refusing this research client) and the FSM immigration site (immigration.gov.fm) doesn't resolve. Salespersons' permits run at most six months each (not a residence route).

sources.title: Permanent Mission of the FSM to the UN: FSM adopts new Immigration Regulation (FSM Information Services, 22 November 2005)
sources.said: The Government of the Federated States of Micronesia has adopted a new immigration regulation, which went into effect October 2005. ... Pursuant to the Compact, as amended, a significant change in the new regulation is that citizens of the US are exempt from all entry permit fees and have the right to reside, work and do business in the FSM without any additional immigration related documents and are not required to register their presence in the FSM. ... The changes include requirements for how a non-citizen may change their entry permit status, some exemptions to the immigration requirements for citizens of the RMI and Palau and a requirement that non-citizens pay fees for entry permits. ... salespersons’ permits, previously issued for one year at a time, will now only be issued for a maximum of six months per permit.
